sections.value:
PR #240 correctness review
Head: 69c0516d8879793b1776753e6d75839931608ce0
Result: pass-with-notes
Request: 01a1eca5-a092-7853-a921-e6792392eea4

No blocking correctness finding in the scoped F198/F195 changes. Source review
covered all 18 changed files and the relevant registration, identity, lease,
rendering and launch-counter call paths. No local Cargo build or test ran.

F198: invocation and identity

- The managed shell script ends in exec pij-rs statusline copilot. A wrapper
  shell between that command and Copilot remains on the ancestry chain, so it
  does not prevent matching the registered host. main.rs passes the statusline
  process's actual PID, not an inherited seat id, into runs_under.
- runs_under checks self and up to 63 ancestors, with at most 64 parent reads
  on a miss. A match also requires that PID's observed local process start to
  equal the recorded start. There is no immediate-parent-only assumption.
  The exact bound is 64 examined PIDs, not acceptance at a 64th parent edge;
  ordinary wrappers fit comfortably within it.
- The native extension records a Copilot host ancestor, and registration
  verifies that process against the same local lstart identity used here.
  The local/UTC pair from observed_start is deliberately reduced to local.
- macOS parent_pid reuses parent_and_name: ProcBSDShortInfo verifies pbsi_pid
  before returning pbsi_ppid. observed_start uses ProcBSDInfo, verifies pbi_pid,
  and converts pbi_start_tvsec using the start instant's local timezone.
  Linux reads PPID field 4 after the last ')' in /proc/PID/stat. These new
  reads call neither Command::new nor the ps fallback in ProcLiveness.
- A foreign PID, a recycled start, missing process evidence or a remote
  descriptor suppresses the identity before rendering. Refusals no longer
  extract or render a seat name from their message. Pane resolution still
  clears inherited PIJ_SESSION_ID; paneless resolution also checks ancestry.
- This is a display brake: removing it can expose more names; it does not
  register, retire, refuse delivery to, or kill a seat. It is not a new
  retention or identity-authority policy. C33 remains the trust boundary.

F195: lease calculation and rendering

- Both additions reuse DeliveryService's existing in-memory lease authority.
  Lease expiry and age use tokio::time::Instant, not wall-clock milliseconds.
  The matching native incarnation's renewal instant supplies the age.
  A missing/incarnation-mismatched renewal does not fabricate a timestamp:
  the card says it has not renewed since daemon start and the list omits age.
- receiver_live's existing boot grace and strict expiry threshold are retained.
  A renewed receiver is excluded on the next read; nothing in this PR latches
  a lapse. The state line is gated by a fresh native_receiver_reason read.
  If expiry occurs between its two reads, the state line can omit "since"
  rather than inventing an age; this is handled explicitly.
- Only native Copilot receivers qualify. The list further gates the suffix to
  local rows and excludes tombstones. Remote rows do not acquire a local
  receiver label. State's reason is likewise restricted to native Copilot.
- The newly generated display values contain fixed text, a numeric duration,
  and one of active/dead/recycled/unbound. They introduce no remote text,
  shell execution, path lookup or unescaped user-controlled field. Both
  roster renderers preserve the existing dialog state and append the suffix.

Evidence and limits

- just pr-freeze 240: FINAL, exact remote/gh head agreement, main base, CLEAN,
  all five checks passed, not draft, no migrations, clean detached checkout.
- CI run 44228256498 is a successful pull_request run for this exact head.
  rust-test: 2441 passed, 6 skipped by nextest's summary. Successful job
  134546668452 uploaded artifact 14394216170; its JUnit has 2441 cases and
  zero failures/errors.
- The artifact explicitly records PASS for the F198 foreign-seat regression,
  real ancestry regression, Linux PPID parser, F195 HTTP lapse regression,
  CLI state rendering regression, statusline golden parity, real-daemon
  statusline integration, and all three spawn-site/path guards.
- Node 22 CI records PASS for generation-routing.test.ts (55 tests) and
  roster-table.test.ts (3 tests); the shared list-sized golden pins the Rust
  and TS roster renderers. Node 22 and 24 typecheck/lint/test jobs are green.
- macOS-only code was inspected by eye, NOT independently compiled or tested
  here. Linux CI is not evidence that the macOS cfg was compiled.
- harness boot --json returned advisory ready:false at worktree-deps because
  this review checkout has no vitest. No dependency installation or symlink
  was made. Local harness checks was not run: it would invoke Cargo/tests
  contrary to the review packet. CI, not a local full-gate claim, is the proof.

Non-blocking notes

- Coverage follow-up, not a merge gate: add to the existing regressions a
  multi-wrapper success case, unavailable ancestor/start reads, the depth
  boundary, never-renewed state/list output, and absence of both labels after
  renewal. The existing renewal assertion checks heartbeat state "live", not
  subsequent card/list output. The TS state test does not yet assert the new
  nativeReceiverLine. The current HTTP test checks prefixes, not an exact
  controlled-clock age. Source supports these paths, but do not claim that
  each is independently pinned by this PR's tests.
- Cost precision: the lease snapshot is O(N), but the added list projection
  finds each local row in a Vec of L lapsed receivers: O(N + N_local * L),
  worst-case quadratic comparisons in memory, not strictly O(N) overall.
  This adds no process launches and is not a demonstrated fleet cost breach.

Cost review and live baseline

- Statusline: every render, configured refresh 10 seconds per visible
  Copilot session. For N rendering sessions this is N/10 existing whoami
  requests per second, with ZERO additional daemon requests per render.
  Added work is at most 64 in-process parent reads plus one start read on a
  matching PID; normally one parent read plus one start read. ZERO added
  launches per render. The existing statusline process and pre-existing git
  fallback are not being counted as zero total OS launches.
- State: one added in-memory lease read for the requested seat per call.
  The shared seat_card also applies this per card in /v1/cards. List: one
  added in-memory lease snapshot per call, then the projection noted above.
  No new poll, timer, renewal-loop change, store read or launch site.
- crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs scans harnesses and daemon production
  code, but not CLI. Its CI pass corroborates the daemon launch inventory;
  direct source inspection establishes zero launches on the new CLI path.
- Measured BEFORE deployment, 2026-11-18 03:14:46Z to 03:15:06Z:
  pij-rs --json ping | jq .data.spawns returned total 793 at both endpoints.
  Every by_op counter was unchanged: 0 launches/20 seconds, 0.0 launches/s.
  Snapshot at both endpoints:
  ddocs.community=68; gh.delivered=1; git.community=241;
  git.pa-watchdog-common-dir=31; ps.registration-native-process=152;
  ps.sidecar-process-group=1; ps.tmux-harness-process-tree=14;
  sh.background-job=3; tmux.atomically reserve staged submit=1;
  tmux.authorize staged submit commit=1; tmux.control-client=1;
  tmux.load submit buffer=3; tmux.new-window=11;
  tmux.paste owned submit buffer=3; tmux.pipe-pane attach=121;
  tmux.pipe-pane detach=2; tmux.rename-window=16;
  tmux.restore pane input and release ownership=1;
  tmux.set-options tap owner=121; tmux.submit authorized staged body=1.
- just spawn-rate --seconds 20 succeeded: 167.1 whole-machine new processes/s,
  156.0 sampled/s; daemon children lower-bound attribution empty, statusline
  runs observed 0.0/s. This observational sample does not prove a future

  Daemon PID 46800: ps reported 12.1% CPU and RSS 143136 KiB.

Owed after merge/reinstall/bounce

Repeat both cost instruments over a known interval on the deployed head,
including daemon CPU/RSS. Confirm a second-server unregistered Copilot never
shows the main-server seat, a registered Copilot still shows itself, and an
expired native receiver is visible in both state and list and clears after
renewal. The baseline above is not after-deploy evidence.
